name: a low-confidence OCR-derived health state must not auto-supersede a confident prior
description: docs/reference/ANALYSIS.md 'Guards': low-confidence numeric health facts never auto-supersede anything. Note 1 records a confident medication regimen (lisinopril, conf 0.95). Note 2 is a blurry OCR read the model returns at conf 0.25. Even though the OCR text is surface-attested (so the weight model would commit it), supersession.decide()'s low-confidence guard is keyed on the model's SELF-confidence, not the plan weight: a 0.25 read that would supersede a more-confident active fact is parked as pending_review behind a low_confidence card, and the confident fact stays active. Pins that a blurry OCR value can't silently overwrite a confident fact (regression: integrate must thread self-confidence to decide(), not the plan weight a surface-attested fact carries).
xfail: SAFETY gap, and the only scenario in the corpus that asserts a `low_confidence` card. The tool surface has no confidence field and `assert_fact` stamps `self_confidence=1.0` on every fact, so the model's own 0.25 self-report is inexpressible — and `supersession.decide`'s low-confidence guard is keyed on exactly that field (`candidate.self_confidence < LOW_CONFIDENCE`), so the whole branch is unreachable from a tool write. The failure is in the DANGEROUS direction: a blurry OCR read of a blood-pressure medication overwrites a 0.95-confidence prior with no card and no held row. Closing it needs a channel for model self-confidence (a tool field, or a derivation the write path trusts), not a `kind` field — this reason previously blamed the missing `kind`, which is a separate, milder gap and is not what fails here.

steps.body: Confirmed with Dr. Okafor: I'm on lisinopril 10mg daily.
Photo of the pharmacy label (blurry OCR): looks like it might say losartan 50mg?

facts.statement: Pharmacy label (OCR, low confidence) reads losartan 50mg daily.
